name: Web Application Security
tagline: Intercepting proxies, content discovery, injection testing, and API tooling for authorized web assessments.

tools.name: Burp Suite
tools.desc: The de-facto intercepting proxy: intercept and edit requests, inspect responses, map the app, and extend workflows with a large marketplace.
tools.when: When you need to manually inspect and shape every request against an app you're authorized to test, or want Professional-grade scanning and macro-based session handling.

tools.name: OWASP ZAP
tools.desc: Free and open-source OWASP proxy with automated scanning, a baseline API for CI, fuzzing, and a REST API for integration.
tools.when: When Burp is not an option due to licensing or budget, or you want scriptable scanning you can drive from a pipeline against a staging app you own.

tools.name: Caido
tools.desc: Lightweight, modern intercepting proxy with a clean UI and fast request replay, built as a slim alternative to the heavyweight suites.
tools.when: When you want a quick, single-file proxy for interception and replay without a large install footprint.
tools.install: brew tap caido/caido && brew install caido

tools.name: ffuf
tools.desc: High-speed Go web fuzzer handling directory, virtual-host, parameter, and header fuzzing over reusable wordlists and encoders.
tools.when: Your default content-discovery engine on an authorized target: large wordlists, vhost fuzzing, and parameter guessing.

tools.name: gobuster
tools.desc: Lightweight Go brute-forcer for directories/files, DNS subdomains, and virtual hosts using custom wordlists.
tools.when: When you need a single-binary directory scan with zero dependencies, or a quick DNS or vhost brute force.

tools.name: feroxbuster
tools.desc: Rust-based recursive content scanner that follows discovered paths automatically and color-codes results by status.
tools.when: When recursive crawling of your own app's content tree matters more than raw wordlist throughput.

tools.name: dirsearch
tools.desc: Python directory brute-forcer with a built-in wordlist, recursive mode, and extension/status filters to cut noise.
tools.when: When you want a battery-included scanner with sane defaults against a single host.

tools.name: wfuzz
tools.desc: Flexible Python web fuzzer built on curl backends; supports multiple payload injection points and fine-grained response matching.
tools.when: When you need to fuzz several positions (headers, cookies, parameters) in one request with precise match filters.

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.desc: Automated SQL injection engine supporting boolean, time-based, error, union, and stacked techniques plus database fingerprinting.
tools.when: After a parameter in an app you're authorized to test looks injectable — it automates detection and database fingerprinting in one pass.
alt: manual payload probes via Burp Repeater

tools.name: NoSQLMap
tools.desc: Automated NoSQL database testing (MongoDB, CouchDB) focused on enumeration, injection, and blind testing of document-store backends.
tools.when: When the API you're testing is backed by a document store and classic SQL payloads don't apply.
tools.install: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/codingo/NoSQLMap.git && cd NoSQLMap && python3 setup.py install

tools.name: Dalfox
tools.desc: Go-based XSS scanner that runs a fast analysis pass, sends crafted payloads, and confirms findings with headless-browser verification.
tools.when: When you want automated, verifiable XSS coverage across many endpoints in a target you're authorized to test.
alt: manual encoding checks via Burp Proxy

tools.name: XSStrike
tools.desc: Python XSS test suite with context-aware payload crafting, filter-detection heuristics, and a small built-in fuzzing engine.
tools.when: When straight payloads fail and you need context-aware payload generation to understand why a filter rejected them.

tools.name: mitmproxy
tools.desc: Interactive HTTPS proxy with a Python addon API for scripting request transformations, plus replay and mock flows for API traffic.
tools.when: When you need scriptable request manipulation, or want to log, inspect, and replay API traffic headlessly.

tools.name: Postman
tools.desc: API client for organizing requests into collections, environment variables, and automated test runners; surfaces contract and auth issues early.
tools.when: During development of your own service for functional API exploration, regression checks, and documenting expected behavior.

tools.name: httpie
tools.desc: Human-friendly HTTP client with readable colored output, JSON-first rewriting, and simple chaining of requests in the shell.
tools.when: When you want a quick one-liner API check without opening an app or writing verbose curl flags.

tools.name: Commix
tools.desc: Automates detection of command injection flaws in arbitrary request fields using time- and output-based techniques plus filter-bypass payloads.
tools.when: When a parameter in an authorized target appears to reach a shell (ping, logs, filename inputs) and you want automated confirmation.
alt: manual output/time-based probes via Burp Repeater
ffuf for payload fuzzing at the field

tools.name: jwt_tool
tools.desc: JWT audit toolkit that checks common misconfigurations: algorithm confusion, weak signing keys, and expired/mis-set claims.
tools.when: When the app under test uses JWTs and you want to audit key handling, which algorithms it accepts, and token lifetime settings.

tools.name: smuggler
tools.desc: HTTP request-smuggling detector that fuzzes CL/TE header combinations against a host and reports which parsing behavior won.
tools.when: When you control the web server stack and want to verify front/back-end header-parsing consistency on permitted infrastructure.
alt: manual CL/TE shaping in Burp Repeater
